question: WAN in the context of computers and networking stands for:
solution:
The correct answer is __Wide Area Network.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• WAN: 

 
 
• A wide area network (WAN) is a large computer network that connects groups of computers over large distances.
 
• WANs are often used by large businesses to connect their office networks; each office typically has its own local area network or LAN, and these are LANs connected via a WAN. These long connections may be formed in several different ways, including leased lines, VPNs, or IP tunnels.
 
• The Internet itself is considered a WAN.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• LAN:

 
 
• It stands for Local Area Network.
 
• A local area network (LAN) consists of a series of computers linked together to form a network in a circumscribed location.
 
• The computers in a LAN connection to each other via TCP/IP ethernet or Wi-Fi.
 
• A LAN is normally exclusive to an organization, such as a school, office, association, or church.
 
 
 
• MAN:
 
 
• It stands for metropolitan area network.
 
• The word MAN refers to merging several local area networks (LANs) in a city into a single, more extensive network that may connect to a vast area network efficiently.
 
• A MAN is larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.
